meta.title: The Complete System Design Path — Free Interactive Edition
meta.subtitle: An independent, offline study edition inspired by the public sys0 syllabus.

modules.title: What is system design?
modules.summary: The choices you make when building a system.

lessons.title: What system design means
lessons.summary: The choices you make when building a system.

lessons.title: The design process
lessons.summary: How one sentence in a meeting becomes a line of code.

lessons.title: Functional vs non-functional requirements
lessons.summary: Nobody hands you a list of requirements. Here's how to find them.

lessons.title: Everything is a tradeoff
lessons.summary: Every choice gives something up. Here's how to choose.

lessons.title: Lab: Design system for a clinic
lessons.summary: A doctor wants online booking. Find out what she actually needs.

modules.title: Start with a simple system
modules.summary: One client, one server, one database. Design its API and its data before anything else.

lessons.title: From requirements to requests
lessons.summary: Three requirements, more than a dozen requests. Here's how to find them.

lessons.title: Data modeling
lessons.summary: Code gets rewritten. Data stays. Here's how to shape it.

lessons.title: Indexes
lessons.summary: Your API tells you which lookups run most. Index those, check the plan with EXPLAIN - and see what every index costs your writes.

lessons.title: Designing the API
lessons.summary: A few basic rules that make an API easy to use and easy to change.

lessons.title: Choosing a database
lessons.summary: What each kind of database gives up, and how to pick one for your app.

lessons.title: Reverse proxy
lessons.summary: What a reverse proxy is, and why we put one in front of our API server.

lessons.title: How do you know it's working?
lessons.summary: Turn "fast" and "always up" into numbers you can measure: p99 instead of the average, error rate, and how close each part is to its limit.

lessons.title: Proof: load testing one server
lessons.summary: We built it in Go and load-tested it from another machine. Where one server breaks - before and after the index.

lessons.title: Lab: Design the clinic's API and data
lessons.summary: Turn the clinic's requests into an API, then into tables and indexes.

modules.title: Caching
modules.summary: Cache the data you read often, so the database isn't queried every time - and keep the cache from serving stale data.

lessons.title: Why cache, and what
lessons.summary: Hits, misses and TTL. Cache only when you must, and pick data by how often it changes.

lessons.title: Where the cache lives
lessons.summary: In-process or a cache server like Redis - and why one server needs nothing more than the first.

lessons.title: Reading and writing with a cache
lessons.summary: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through and refresh-ahead - and why the database is written first.

lessons.title: Cache invalidation
lessons.summary: TTLs and invalidating on write. Cache data to show it, but check the database before you act on it.

lessons.title: When the cache is full
lessons.summary: LRU, LFU and the rest. Watch the hit rate and the eviction rate to see if your cache is working.

lessons.title: When caching makes things worse
lessons.summary: Keys that expire together, a hot key that expires, lookups for data that doesn't exist - and the fix for each.

lessons.title: Proof: the menu page with a cache
lessons.summary: The same load test with and without the cache: requests per second, p99, database CPU and hit rate. Then every key expires at once.

lessons.title: Lab: What can the clinic cache?
lessons.summary: Cache the doctor list. Never the free slots - a stale slot is a double booking.

modules.title: When one server isn't enough
modules.summary: Dinner traffic outgrows one server. Scale vertically, then horizontally, and fix what breaks on server two.

lessons.title: Vertical scaling
lessons.summary: Our load test found where one server breaks. The first fix is a bigger machine - and it has a ceiling.

lessons.title: Horizontal scaling
lessons.summary: More machines instead of a bigger one: no ceiling, and no single server to lose - but now there are two.

lessons.title: Load balancers
lessons.summary: A reverse proxy with more than one server behind it: how it picks a server, what happens when one dies - and why the balancer can't be a single point of failure.

lessons.title: Stateless servers
lessons.summary: Why a login breaks on server two, and where sessions, cache and photos go instead.

lessons.title: Connection pooling
lessons.summary: Every server opens its own database connections. Add servers and you hit the database's limit while it's barely busy - pools and database proxies.

lessons.title: Object storage: where the photos go
lessons.summary: Dish photos don't belong on a server's disk or in the database. A bucket holds them, and the app uploads straight to it.

lessons.title: CDN: a cache near the user
lessons.summary: Serve menu photos from close to the customer, not from your servers.

lessons.title: Proof: two servers behind a load balancer
lessons.summary: The load test that broke one server, run again against two. What doubled, and what didn't.

lessons.title: Lab: Does the clinic need a second server?
lessons.summary: The Monday 9am rush, a $50 budget, and the numbers that decide.

modules.title: When one database isn't enough
modules.summary: The servers scale out, but every query still goes to one database. Add read replicas, then deal with what copies bring: lag, failover, backups and recovery.

lessons.title: Read replicas
lessons.summary: Our load test's next limit is the database. Keep writes on one primary, copy it, and send reads to the copies.

lessons.title: Replication lag
lessons.summary: Copies fall behind the primary. Why a customer can't find the order they just placed, and how to read your own writes.

lessons.title: When the primary dies
lessons.summary: Promote a replica: automatic or manual, the writes you can lose, and what “three nines” really allows.

lessons.title: Backups and recovery
lessons.summary: A replica copies your mistakes too. Backups, point-in-time restore, and testing that a restore works.

lessons.title: Proof: one primary, two replicas
lessons.summary: The load test that maxed out one database, run again with two replicas. Then we kill the primary and time the failover.

lessons.title: Lab: Add read replicas to the clinic
lessons.summary: The database is the bottleneck. Add replicas, handle replication lag, and plan failover and backups.

modules.title: Live updates
modules.summary: Some news can't wait for the app to ask. Choose between asking often and keeping a connection open - and make it work across many servers.

lessons.title: Polling, SSE, WebSockets, push
lessons.summary: Ask every few seconds, or keep a connection open. Four ways to get news to the restaurant and the customer, what each costs the server, and why polling is often enough.

lessons.title: Live updates across many servers
lessons.summary: The restaurant's tablet is connected to server 1, but the new order lands on server 2. Redis pub/sub joins them. And when the tablet's Wi-Fi drops, it fetches what it missed from the database - the push is fast, the database is the truth.

lessons.title: Proof: 10,000 order screens
lessons.summary: Load-test 10,000 open order screens asking every 5 seconds, then holding one connection each. Then send a new order through two servers, and cut a tablet's connection mid-rush.

lessons.title: Lab: Add live updates to the clinic
lessons.summary: Tell patients in the waiting room the moment Dr. Rao is running late - from any server, without them refreshing.

modules.title: Background jobs
modules.summary: Not everything has to happen before the response. Move slow work to a queue and workers - and make sure a job that runs twice does no harm.

lessons.title: Why the user shouldn't wait
lessons.summary: The order is slow because of an SMS the customer didn't need yet. Which work must happen before the response, and which can happen after.

lessons.title: A queue in the database you have
lessons.summary: A jobs table and a worker that polls it. Why two workers grab the same job, and how row locks and SKIP LOCKED stop it. Often all you need.

lessons.title: Queues and workers
lessons.summary: Our database is already the busiest part, so jobs move to a dedicated queue. Producers, workers, and a queue that absorbs the dinner spike.

lessons.title: When a job fails
lessons.summary: A slow SMS provider now holds up workers instead of customers, and the queue piles up. Timeouts, retries with backoff, acknowledgements, and idempotent workers - because a job can run twice. And a dead-letter queue for jobs that never succeed.

lessons.title: Proof: take the SMS out of the order
lessons.summary: Load-test orders with a slow SMS provider, then with a queue. Then kill a worker mid-refund and count the refunds, with and without an idempotency key.

lessons.title: Lab: Add a queue to the clinic
lessons.summary: Send the day-before appointment reminders through a queue and workers - every one on time, and none twice.

modules.title: Rate limiting
modules.summary: Not every request deserves a reply. Decide how much each client may ask for, and keep that limit across many servers.

lessons.title: Why limit requests
lessons.summary: Bots, buggy apps and one greedy client. Who to limit (user, IP, API key), what to send back (429 and Retry-After), and where the limit lives.

lessons.title: Counting requests
lessons.summary: Fixed window and the burst at its edge, sliding window, and token bucket - which lets a real user burst a little.

lessons.title: One limit across many servers
lessons.summary: Three servers counting alone allow three times the limit. One counter in Redis, updated in one step so two servers can't both slip through.

lessons.title: Proof: stop the OTP flood
lessons.summary: Flood the login from another machine and count the SMS sent: no limit, a limit on each server, then one limit in Redis.

lessons.title: Lab: Add rate limits to the clinic
lessons.summary: Stop bots grabbing every Monday slot, without blocking patients who book honestly.

modules.title: Growing big
modules.summary: Years of data, many cities, many teams. The cheap steps first - archive and partition - then the two hardest ones, put off as long as you can.

lessons.title: Old data you rarely read
lessons.summary: Almost every query asks about this week. Move old orders to cheap storage, and keep what the law says you must keep.

lessons.title: Partitioning a table
lessons.summary: Split the orders table by month inside one database. Removing a month becomes instant instead of one huge DELETE - and why it barely speeds up a query that already has an index.

lessons.title: Sharding
lessons.summary: When one machine can't hold it: split the data by city across databases. What a shard key is, what you lose (a query across all cities), and why it comes last. The deep dive is in Part 2.

lessons.title: Splitting into services
lessons.summary: Microservices solve a people problem. Here's how to tell when you have it, and what it costs - like following one slow order across five services.

lessons.title: Proof: clear out an old month
lessons.summary: Every month the oldest orders move to the archive. Remove one month from 30 million orders twice - row by row, then by dropping its partition - while new orders keep coming in. Compare the time, the new orders' speed, and the disk freed.

lessons.title: Lab: Ten years of clinic bookings
lessons.summary: 400 clinics and ten years of appointments. Archive the old ones and split the rest by month - then decide whether it needs shards. (It doesn't.)

modules.title: Putting it together
modules.summary: Design a whole system from a blank page, and explain your choices out loud.

lessons.title: The design interview
lessons.summary: It's the design process from Module 1, done in 45 minutes.

lessons.title: Back-of-the-envelope estimation
lessons.summary: Turn users into requests per second, storage and bandwidth - fast enough to do in an interview.

lessons.title: Drawing it and talking tradeoffs
lessons.summary: Never say “the best”. Say what you chose, what you gave up, and why.

lessons.title: Capstone: Design the whole app
lessons.summary: The food delivery app, from requirements to fifty cities, on your own.

modules.title: Microservices
modules.summary: Splitting the app into services: where to draw the boundaries, how services call each other, and how to trace a request across them.

lessons.title: Service boundaries
lessons.summary: Split by business capability, not by table. Each service owns its data, and other services don't read its database.

lessons.title: Synchronous vs asynchronous calls
lessons.summary: Use a direct call when you need the answer before replying, and a queue when you don't. Payment needs an answer; sending an SMS doesn't.

lessons.title: REST vs gRPC
lessons.summary: REST and JSON for public APIs, gRPC with a shared schema between services, and the tradeoffs of each.

lessons.title: API gateway and service discovery
lessons.summary: A single entry point for the apps, and how services find each other when instances are added and removed.

lessons.title: Backend for frontend
lessons.summary: The customer app, the restaurant tablet and the rider app need different data. A separate backend for each client, and when one gateway is enough.

lessons.title: Aggregating data from several services
lessons.summary: The order page needs data from the order, restaurant and rider services. Call them in parallel, combine the results, and decide what to return when one of them fails.

lessons.title: Authentication across services
lessons.summary: The auth service signs a JWT with its private key (RS256), and every other service checks it with the public key from a JWKS endpoint - no call to the auth service per request. Key rotation, and how services authenticate each other.

lessons.title: Distributed tracing
lessons.summary: Pass one request ID through every call, and use traces to find which service made an order slow.

lessons.title: Proof: one process vs five services
lessons.summary: Place an order in one process, then across five services. Compare latency and find the slow call in the trace.

lessons.title: Lab: Split the order flow
lessons.summary: Design the services for ordering, payment and dispatch, and choose how each pair communicates.

modules.title: Problems in distributed systems
modules.summary: Things that work on one machine and fail across many: timeouts, retries, clocks, counters and locks. Each lesson covers the basic fix and points to the module with the full solution.

lessons.title: Partial failure and timeouts
lessons.summary: You can't tell a slow machine from a crashed one. After a timeout, you don't know whether the payment went through.

lessons.title: Retry storms and cascading failures
lessons.summary: When the payment service slows down, every caller retries, and retries multiply at each layer. Backoff, jitter and retry budgets.

lessons.title: Circuit breakers and load shedding
lessons.summary: Stop calling a failing service and return a fallback. Under overload, reject some requests so the rest still succeed.

lessons.title: Tail latency
lessons.summary: A page that calls ten services hits at least one service's p99 on most requests. How fan-out makes tail latency matter.

lessons.title: Clocks and ordering
lessons.summary: Clocks on different machines drift. Last-write-wins can lose updates, and timestamps can't reliably order events.

lessons.title: Duplicate and out-of-order messages
lessons.summary: “Order cancelled” can arrive before “order placed”, and “order paid” can arrive twice. Why this happens, and why handlers must be idempotent.

lessons.title: Inconsistent data
lessons.summary: The order is saved but the “paid” event is never sent. A customer updates their address and the next page shows the old one. Two writes in two places, with no shared transaction.

lessons.title: Counters and limits across machines
lessons.summary: Stock counts that oversell, per-server rate limits that allow too much traffic, and auto-increment IDs that collide.

lessons.title: Locks and leaders
lessons.summary: A lock in one process doesn't protect anything on another machine. A lease can expire during a pause, leaving two machines that both think they're the leader.

lessons.title: Proof: one slow service
lessons.summary: Slow down the payment service under load and measure what retries do to the app. Then add backoff, a circuit breaker and load shedding, and measure again.

lessons.title: Lab: Inject failures into the clinic
lessons.summary: Add latency, stop a machine, skew a clock and split the network. Predict the effect on bookings, then test it.

modules.title: Replication in depth
modules.summary: Keeping copies of data on several machines: replication modes, leader election, consistency, and resolving conflicts.

lessons.title: Sync, async and failover
lessons.summary: What happens when the leader fails: lost writes, split brain and fencing.

lessons.title: Leader election and Raft
lessons.summary: How nodes agree on a leader and a log, and why you use etcd or ZooKeeper instead of implementing it.

lessons.title: Consistency models
lessons.summary: Read-your-writes, monotonic reads, linearizability and eventual consistency, with examples from the app.

lessons.title: Leaderless and quorums
lessons.summary: Dynamo-style replication: R + W > N, and what it does and doesn't guarantee.

lessons.title: Conflict resolution
lessons.summary: Last-write-wins, version vectors and CRDTs.

lessons.title: CAP and PACELC
lessons.summary: What CAP says and doesn't say, and the latency vs consistency tradeoff you make every day.

lessons.title: Lab: Choose consistency levels
lessons.summary: Menu, cart, payment, rider location: choose a consistency level for each and justify it.

modules.title: Partitioning in depth
modules.summary: Splitting data across machines while avoiding hot spots, expensive queries and costly rebalancing.

lessons.title: Range vs hash partitioning
lessons.summary: How each method splits the data, and what it does to your queries.

lessons.title: Consistent hashing
lessons.summary: Add a machine and move only a small part of the data.

lessons.title: Hot keys
lessons.summary: When one key gets most of the traffic, like a very popular restaurant.

lessons.title: Queries across shards
lessons.summary: Secondary indexes, scatter-gather and request routing.

lessons.title: IDs without a central counter
lessons.summary: Snowflake IDs, UUIDs, and why order sometimes matters.

lessons.title: Lab: Reshard without downtime
lessons.summary: Add shards under live traffic without losing orders.

modules.title: Messaging: Kafka and pub/sub
modules.summary: Services publish events instead of calling each other in a chain: pub/sub, Kafka, fan-out and delivery guarantees.

lessons.title: Pub/sub
lessons.summary: The order service publishes “order placed” without knowing which services consume it.

lessons.title: How Kafka works
lessons.summary: Topics, partitions and offsets, and why reading a message doesn't delete it.

lessons.title: Kafka as a queue
lessons.summary: Consumer groups split the work, the partition count limits how many consumers you can run, and slow consumers build up lag.

lessons.title: Fan-out and fan-in
lessons.summary: Sending one event to many services, and combining several events into one result, such as waiting for payment and restaurant confirmation before assigning a rider.

lessons.title: Message ordering
lessons.summary: Kafka keeps order only within a partition. Choose the key so all events for one order go to the same partition.

lessons.title: At most, at least, exactly once
lessons.summary: What a message system can guarantee, and why exactly-once in practice means idempotent consumers.

lessons.title: Lab: Event-driven order flow
lessons.summary: Connect order, payment and rider services with events, then take one down.

modules.title: Transactions across services
modules.summary: Placing an order writes to three services. How to keep them consistent when any of them can fail partway through.

lessons.title: Isolation levels
lessons.summary: Lost updates and write skew within one database, before adding more.

lessons.title: Outbox and change data capture
lessons.summary: Save to the database and publish an event reliably, without losing either.

lessons.title: Two-phase commit
lessons.summary: Commit across two databases, why it can get stuck, and why services rarely use it.

lessons.title: Sagas
lessons.summary: A sequence of local transactions with compensating steps: refund the payment if no restaurant accepts the order.

lessons.title: Locks, leases and fencing tokens
lessons.summary: Distributed locks with etcd or ZooKeeper, and fencing tokens to make them safe.

lessons.title: Lab: Order saga
lessons.summary: Run an order across payment, restaurant and rider services, crash each one in turn, and make sure no customer is charged for an order that won't be delivered.

modules.title: Events and streams
modules.summary: Event sourcing, CQRS, stream processing and batch processing.

lessons.title: Event sourcing and CQRS
lessons.summary: Store every change as an event instead of only the current state, and when not to.

lessons.title: Stream processing
lessons.summary: Windows, late events and aggregating data as it arrives.

lessons.title: Batch and analytics
lessons.summary: OLTP vs OLAP, data warehouses, and running reports without slowing down orders.

lessons.title: Lab: Live orders per city
lessons.summary: Count orders per city as they arrive, handling late and duplicate events, and compare the result with the nightly batch.

modules.title: Availability and going global
modules.summary: Setting an uptime target, what each extra nine costs, and running in multiple regions.

lessons.title: Availability and the nines
lessons.summary: 99.9% allows about nine hours of downtime a year, 99.99% under one. How components in series lower availability, and how redundancy raises it.

lessons.title: Multi-region
lessons.summary: Active-passive vs active-active, and where writes go.

lessons.title: Geo-routing
lessons.summary: How DNS, anycast and edge locations route each user to the nearest region.

lessons.title: Disaster recovery
lessons.summary: RPO, RTO, cross-region backups and chaos testing.

lessons.title: Lab: Region failover
lessons.summary: Fail over a whole region and measure the data lost.

modules.title: Classic algorithms in action
modules.summary: The algorithms under every big system, as simulations: run them, break them, and see why they work.

lessons.title: Consistent hashing
lessons.summary: Add a server to the ring and watch which keys move - then add virtual nodes.

lessons.title: Bloom filter
lessons.summary: “Definitely not” or “maybe”: tune its size and count the false positives.

lessons.title: HyperLogLog
lessons.summary: Count millions of unique visitors in 12 KB of memory.

lessons.title: Count-min sketch and top-K
lessons.summary: Find tonight's trending dishes without counting every one exactly.

lessons.title: Geohash and quadtree
lessons.summary: Find the nearest rider without checking every rider in the city.

lessons.title: Trie
lessons.summary: Autocomplete: suggestions after every letter typed.

lessons.title: Inverted index
lessons.summary: How search finds every menu with “paneer” in it.

lessons.title: B-tree vs LSM tree
lessons.summary: Two ways to store data on disk: fast reads or fast writes.

lessons.title: Write-ahead log
lessons.summary: Crash the database mid-write, then watch it recover.

lessons.title: Merkle tree
lessons.summary: Find what differs between two replicas without comparing everything.

lessons.title: Snowflake IDs
lessons.summary: Unique, sortable IDs from many machines - until a clock jumps back.

lessons.title: Lamport and vector clocks
lessons.summary: Put events in order when no clock can be trusted.

lessons.title: Gossip and failure detection
lessons.summary: How a cluster spreads news and notices a dead machine.

lessons.title: Quorum reads and writes
lessons.summary: Change N, R and W, kill a node, and see what readers get.

lessons.title: Raft
lessons.summary: Elect a leader, replicate a log, then cut the network.

lessons.title: Leases and fencing tokens
lessons.summary: A paused lock holder wakes up and tries to write.

lessons.title: CRDTs
lessons.summary: Two offline phones edit the same cart. Merge them without losing anything.

lessons.title: Fan-out on write vs read
lessons.summary: Post as a celebrity with 10 million followers, and watch the feed build.

lessons.title: Sharded counters
lessons.summary: Count a million likes a second without one hot row.
